title: Shared planner authority and workspace isolation
summary: Give every local worktree one planner authority and an explicit independent code/runtime binding.
description:
Give every local worktree one planner authority and an explicit independent code/runtime binding.

Current state: MCP, Pi and CLI default to cwd/.planner. PlanStore already discovers git-common-dir for allocation only; serve.ts derives code root with dirname(store.root). PlanStore.localRoot also houses focus, resumes and session data.

Goals:
- Separate canonical plan identity from workspace/source and caller runtime identity.
- Reuse one coordinated local authority across all supported harnesses.

Responsibilities:
- P128(F025)/T489: Separate planner storage, code workspace and runtime identities. One harness-agnostic resolved binding identifies the canonical plan independently of the selected code checkout and caller runtime.
- P128(F025)/T490: Route all clients through one coordinated local planner authority. Supported MCP, Pi, CLI, server and Web UI consumers use the same local planner authority while keeping code and caller state correctly scoped.

Boundaries:
- No product migration or automatic Git action during planning registration.
- No mandatory cloud service, database or language-specific setup.

Risks:
- Blindly centralizing .local would mix focus, returns and source caches.
- A branch/path locator can change and must not become durable identity.

Acceptance:
- Two local worktrees resolve one project planner and distinct code/runtime contexts; standalone initialization remains usable.
- Moving a worktree or renaming a branch preserves stable identity and history; missing/deleted paths give explicit unavailability.
- Nested repositories/submodules and foreign overrides cannot silently mix source provenance; no language/provider installation is required for planning.
- Concurrent supported host processes observe the same task/decision changes and cannot both successfully claim one task.
- Separate worktrees retain independent focus, resumes and source caches; crash/restart does not transfer a live foreign claim or discard pending returns.
- Stale revisions, repeated requests, incompatible clients and unavailable authority return explicit non-success without duplicate writes or parallel planners.

Preserve canonical UUIDs/shortIds and variable-width references, single-owner Accepted Decisions, phase-scoped handoffs, derived parent status, atomic task/session ownership, explicit recovery, global feature -> phase -> task priority and the accepted warning-only no-task guard. Read current sources, existing precedents and applicable Project Guidelines before coding. Use checklist steps rather than creating tasks per step. Cross-cutting consistency and bounded-cost acceptance (21 October 2026):
Every create/update/move or relationship change checks affected task/phase/feature/project scope and dependency readiness through P128(F025)/T496. Update genuinely obsolete facts only; reviewed-unchanged assessments name exact revisions, and pending semantic obligations remain explicit and resumable. Return indexed affected deltas rather than full ancestor/plan/graph reloads; measure per-flow context/payload/tool budgets without dropping mandatory rules or inventing context retention. BR28 and BR29 apply to this phase. Full contract: .planner/docs/agent-brain-impact-reconciliation-and-token-budgets.md. T496 is stable execution task identity moved from its initial draft placement, not a recreated task.

Prerequisite reconciliation: Current prerequisite contract: T489 -> T496 -> T490; T490 also retains its direct T489 dependency. The shared authority consumes the impact primitives rather than requiring a later standards phase.

tasks.title: Route all clients through one coordinated local planner authority
tasks.description:
Outcome: Supported MCP, Pi, CLI, server and Web UI consumers use the same local planner authority while keeping code and caller state correctly scoped.

Existing state: Each host can construct its own PlanStore and per-root writer lock. Existing claims/recovery protect a task only when callers reach the same physical state; server-record discovery is advisory rather than atomic startup exclusion.

Implementation responsibility:
- Implement the resolved binding from M1 and the shared authority/service lifecycle, including atomic startup ownership, compatible discovery, reconnect and typed dead/incompatible/unavailable outcomes.
- Reuse existing transactions and atomic claims; serialize conflicting operations with expected entity revisions, idempotency keys and actor/execution provenance. Independent code work remains parallel; a slow/dead client cannot leave an indefinite write lock.
- Keep global task claims and coordinator ownership shared, but namespace focus, return chains, read/context evidence, source indexes and analysis caches by their explicit workspace/session/revision keys.
- Update all host entry points and source-root consumers, including GET /project; normal planner operations must not fall back to silently creating a fresh cwd/.planner when the bound authority is unavailable.
- Expose stable domain/service APIs and events for later source and provider brokers. K2 still owns language-server lifecycle and document overlays; sharing planner authority must not launch the dashboard or duplicate the provider broker.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Concurrent supported host processes observe the same task/decision changes and cannot both successfully claim one task.
- Separate worktrees retain independent focus, resumes and source caches; crash/restart does not transfer a live foreign claim or discard pending returns.
- Stale revisions, repeated requests, incompatible clients and unavailable authority return explicit non-success without duplicate writes or parallel planners.

Detailed discussion contract:
- Use a single coordination boundary for planner mutations, with short operation-scoped locks and a recoverable owner. JSON may remain the durable format; this decision does not mandate a database, event-sourcing framework or cloud service.
- A public read must not claim that an arbitrary stored attestation proves the model retained context. Shared storage does not make caller context interchangeable.
- A .planner symlink or AGENT_PLAN_ROOT override alone cannot meet this task: source-root inference, runtime scoping, startup races, incompatible clients and failures must be handled.

tasks.title: Reconcile affected hierarchy and dependencies with bounded context cost
tasks.description:
Outcome: Every planner mutation keeps affected hierarchy and dependency context consistent through one explicit postcondition protocol, with measured bounded agent-context cost.

Existing state: packages/plan-core/src/description-freshness.ts:94 computes timestamp-based phase/feature prose freshness; it does not cover project prose, dependency-impact semantics or an enforced mutation/reconciliation lifecycle. packages/plan-core/planner-skill.md:131 already tells agents to reconcile parents, but the user reports it is not reliably followed. PlanStore.runBatch at packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts:1077 and write coordination are existing extension points; do not recreate a parallel planner.

Implementation responsibility:
- Extend the existing description-freshness, transaction and rule/skill contracts; classify each create/update/move/status/priority/dependency/requirement/decision change by actual semantic impact, not generic updatedAt.
- Compute a bounded affected set from maintained parent/reverse-dependency/link indexes: owning phase/feature/project, old and new parents on moves, incoming/outgoing dependencies and affected readiness/context projections. Do not scan or reload unrelated project content on every write.
- Recompute structural relations and derived rollups within the coordinated mutation; reject dangling references, parent mismatches and dependency cycles with typed diagnostics, without inventing dependencies or cascading task-status changes.
- Assess parent prose and linked/dependent descriptions against changed facts. Apply a minimal factual update through the canonical owner only where necessary; preserve decisions, rationale, user prose and unrelated content. Otherwise record a version-bound no-change-needed assessment, not a cosmetic rewrite.
- Return a compact change-impact receipt containing changed IDs/revisions, relevant before/after facts, affected parents/dependencies and reconciliation outcomes. If semantic review needs an agent/user, persist a durable bounded obligation and return reconciliation_required; do not claim the full operation is reconciled merely because the leaf write persisted.
- Provide expected-revision/idempotent reconcile operations and paginated impact continuation. Concurrent changes invalidate stale assessments, interrupted clients resume obligations, and phase/feature closeout verifies required reconciliation or an explicit recorded unresolved blocker.
- Expose the same domain postconditions through supported MCP/Pi/CLI/server/UI surfaces and D2 portable skills; normal reads are non-mutating, no-task behavior remains warning-only, and a missing agent hook cannot be advertised as enforced interception.
- Measure A2-defined per-flow payload/token and tool-call budgets using fixed fixtures. Reuse already delivered unchanged mandatory context, return affected deltas by default and request full content only on cache/context loss or explicit drill-down; large impact uses bounded continuation without hiding required context.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Creating/updating/moving a task or changing an edge leaves all affected structural parents/dependencies consistent, with a factual prose update or explicit revision-bound reviewed-unchanged/pending result.
- Task -> phase -> feature -> project scope changes reconcile only affected meaning; a new task cannot silently leave contradictory parent descriptions. Edge removal, cross-phase links, deletion/move and concurrent edits are covered.
- A local mutation has bounded incremental response/tool overhead independent of unrelated plan growth; high-fan-out changes paginate explicitly and cached no-op operations do not reload full ancestors/graph.
- Required rules/requirements/decisions remain available after compaction or workspace change; token economy never relies on a stored timestamp as proof of effective model context or silently drops mandatory content.

Detailed contract: structural updates and semantic review are distinct. A write may be persisted while reconciliation remains required; the response must say so and preserve the obligation. Do not blindly rewrite every ancestor, auto-change Accepted Decisions, infer new work dependencies from graph/code links or block unrelated tasks for a local edit. Assess old/new parents and both directions of actual dependency effects. A reviewed-unchanged receipt must name the source/parent revisions and cannot be satisfied by merely touching a timestamp. The no-task guard remains warning-only; this is a planner consistency postcondition, not a newly authorized source-write denial policy.

Ownership: this task owns mutation-impact and reconciliation contracts. G3 reuses them for source/context freshness; B1 consumes updated readiness; C2 owns context delivery/reuse; D2 owns portable skill distribution; I1/I2 own complete and fresh-installed closeout. Exact field/tool names and numeric per-flow budgets are selected from measured A2 baselines, not fabricated promises. All F025 improvements, including shared planner, graph and editor, must meet the common bounded-cost contract.
